title: Improving General Role-Playing Agents via Psychology-Grounded Reasoning and Role-Aware Policy Optimization
claim: Standard group-relative policy optimization treats all tokens alike; ours reweights token-level gradients by profile-induced entropy differences and advantage sign.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow on top, zoomed-in detail below
description: A large two-tier diagram. The top panel shows the sampling stage. A Psy-CoT example about Bellatrix and Snape is on the left, and an Input box holds a role profile, history and initial scene. This feeds a policy model robot, which produces N stacked completions, each split into a Psy-CoT block and an Answer block. A reward model robot and a reference model robot sit beside them. Think, Answer and Format scores feed rewards R1 to RN. Group computation turns those into trophy-icon advantages A1 to AN, which feed a Token Level Loss box. A dashed zoom line leads to the bottom panel. There, the same completion is run with and without the role profile, and the resulting per-token entropies are subtracted. The entropy difference sets a weight W for each token. Scale icons show W>1 or W<1 for role-specific tokens, split by positive or negative advantage. Grey marks general tokens, green and red mark role-specific tokens.
caption: Overview of RAPO. The upper part illustrates the sampling stage: given an input sample, the policy model rolls out multiple completions, each of which is scored by the reward function, and group-relative advantages are then computed. The lower part depicts the token-level gradient modulation applied to each completion, where role-agnostic and role-specific tokens receive differentiated gradient signals conditioned on the sign of the advantage.
abstract: Building general-purpose role-playing agents that faithfully portray any character from a natural-language profile remains challenging. Explicit reasoning can help models deliberate before responding, but generic reasoning does not necessarily preserve character fidelity. We therefore propose Psy-CoT, a psychology-grounded chain-of-thought framework that decomposes pre-response reasoning into three role-specific steps: Interaction Perception, Psychological Empathy, and Logical Construction, so that the model thinks dynamically from the profile rather than merely mimicking surface patterns. While structured reasoning provides a foundation, it alone is insufficient; reinforcement learning is essential to further align the model with character fidelity. However, we observe that under LLM-based reward models, both generic phrases that hack the reward model and genuinely role-specific phrases receive identical gradient signals. This hacking accumulates over training, misleading the model into treating both as equally optimal choices. To address this, we propose Role-Aware Policy Optimization (RAPO), which uses profile-induced entropy differences to weight gradients asymmetrically, amplifying role-specific tokens under positive advantage while attenuating them under negative advantage. Experiments on CoSER, CharacterBench, and CharacterEval demonstrate that Psy-CoT outperforms existing role-playing CoT methods, and RAPO consistently surpasses GRPO across multiple model scales.
